response:
Diagnosis before proposing:

Generation 6 sharpened the picture considerably. QualityAugmentedHarvest is now the best signal on economic magnitude and risk-adjusted terms (fmb 5.23, alpha **6.9%**, t 4.15, Sharpe **0.648**) but sits at coverage 0.081 — exactly the `oancf` sample. HarvestAndIntangibleTilt remains the best coverage-adjusted result (5.3%, t 4.98, Sharpe 0.46, coverage 0.121). Two clean negative results: adding the capex *trend* as a fourth channel diluted rather than helped (5.3% → 4.7%), so the level and slope of reinvestment are largely redundant; and WeakestLinkHarvest collapsed to 0.1%, showing that MIN-based conjunctive gating compresses the cross-section into ties and destroys the spread — averaging ranks is the right aggregator. Industry-neutralizing the R&D tilt preserved a 4.0% alpha with t 4.21, so the intangible channel is *not* merely a sector bet, though the raw version is stronger. External-financing restraint (sstk + aqc) diluted the score to 2.1%; the financing dimension is settled as unhelpful. Real-input breadth (employment) held up (3.9%, t 3.88, Sharpe 0.44).

The critical unresolved question is whether QualityAugmentedHarvest's jump to 6.9% comes from the accrual-quality *channel* or merely from restricting the sample to cash-flow reporters. This batch answers that with a matched control, repairs the quality channel's coverage with an economically justified fallback accrual measure, tests whether the profitability level is redundant once quality is present, and explores one genuinely new intangible dimension (organization capital in SG&A).

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: BroadQualityHarvest
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(COALESCE(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), COALESCE(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(invt, 1), dp), at)))), SUMRANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5)), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Earnings quality can be measured either as the earnings-minus-cash-flow gap or, when cash flow statements are unavailable, as inventory build net of depreciation; either way, cash-backed profits combined with own-history investment restraint and a research-tilted spending mix identify underpriced cash generators.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The quality channel produced the archive's largest alpha and Sharpe but only over the cash-flow-reporting sample, so the fallback balance-sheet accrual proxy is an economically motivated substitute rather than a coverage patch. If the alpha survives at coverage near 0.12, the quality dimension is general; if it fades, the gain was sample-specific and the flagship should stay at three channels.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: CashSampleHarvestControl
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), SUMRANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5)), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash profitability, own-history reinvestment restraint, and research tilt are jointly sufficient; the apparent gain from adding an accrual-gap channel may simply reflect the cash-flow-reporting subsample in which that channel is computable.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is the exact matched control for QualityAugmentedHarvest — same three-channel architecture, same restricted sample, no quality leg — and it is the only way to attribute the 6.9% alpha to a mechanism rather than a sample. The comparison directly determines what the final two generations should refine.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: QualityRestraintTiltNoLevel
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), SUMRANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5)), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Once earnings are known to be cash-backed, the level of profitability adds little: the mispricing is about credibility of profits plus discipline in deploying them, not about the size of the margin.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: In the four-channel quality score the profitability level and the accrual gap both load on cash flow, so they may be partly redundant; dropping the level tests parsimony and tells us whether the profitability *level* or the profitability *quality* is the active ingredient. A strong result here would also mean the signal is nearly orthogonal to RMW, which is the cleanest explanation of the large FF5 alphas in this family.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: OrganizationCapitalTilt
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(COALESCE(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), SUMRANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5)), WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), xsga), ADD(capx, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), xsga))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Intangible investment is broader than R&D: selling, general and administrative spending builds brand, distribution and organizational capital that is expensed rather than capitalized, so profitable firms whose investment is tilted toward intangibles of either kind are systematically underpriced.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The research-tilt channel was the single most valuable addition in the archive (fmb 4.18 alone, and the driver of the 5.3% three-channel alpha), and organization capital is the natural extension of the same mismeasurement mechanism to non-R&D industries. Because SG&A is reported almost universally, this also widens the intangible channel beyond the technology and pharmaceutical firms that dominate R&D reporting.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: PeerRelativeProfitHarvest
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(COALESCE(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), 1)), SUMRANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5)), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)))))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm is a cash cow relative to its industry's economics, so profitability measured against industry peers should identify harvesting candidates more accurately than raw profitability, which mostly ranks industries.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Industry neutralization of the intangible leg preserved the alpha (4.0%, t 4.21), suggesting industry adjustment is safe when applied to a winsorized, bounded quantity; applying it to the profitability leg tests whether within-industry competitive position is the relevant profitability concept. This is the complementary experiment to generation 6's industry test, and unlike the failed IND_ZSCORE investment leg it does not disturb the firm-specific restraint measure.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: BreadthOfExpansionRestraint
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(COALESCE(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), SUMRANK(NEG(SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5), SUMRANK(GROWTH(invt, 1), GROWTH(emp, 1)))), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Discipline is credible when it is broad: profitable firms restraining fixed capital, inventory and headcount simultaneously are genuinely harvesting, whereas restraint in one input alone can be a temporary cash-timing artifact.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The employment-restraint version of this idea worked once measured against the firm's own history (3.9%, t 3.88, Sharpe 0.44), and building a single composite expansion index keeps the added inputs from crowding out the profitability and intangible channels that carry the most alpha. This tests whether breadth of restraint is a better investment leg than capex restraint alone, without disturbing the rest of the winning architecture.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
